newsitem.title: FRANCE: Frenchman jailed over anti-Basque death squads.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman jailed over anti-Basque death squads.

text.p: A French court imposed a 20-year jail sentence on Wednesday on a suspected leader of Spain's "dirty war" against Basques separatist rebels after convicting him of conspiracy and being an accomplice to murder.
In the first French trial of an alleged death squad member, Frenchman Georges Mendaille Georges, 62, was accused of ordering the killing of two Basque refugees in France during the 1980s.

Mendaille, who was extradited from Spain two years ago, denied the charges, insisting instead that he had infiltrated Spain's Anti-Terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL) death squads on behalf of French counter-espionnage services.
His attorney Benoit Ducos-Ader said he would appeal against the verdict, handed down by a special seven-judge anti-terrorist court in Pau near the Franco-Spanish border.
GAL squads killed 28 people between 1983 and 1987, mostly in southern France, in retaliation for killings in Spain by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) separatist guerrillas.
Several top Spanish officials and former security chiefs have been charged with running the death squads.
During Mendaille's trial, prosecutors said Spain had proceeded at a snail's pace in pursuing him. It took eight years from the time that France issued a warrant for his arrest to his extradition.
